chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Regarding the found object (luqata), it is announced for one year, then it becomes like the rest of his wealth.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for a found item (luqata) and how long must it be announced?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the procedure for *al-luqatah* (found property), requiring the finder to publicize the item for a full year. If the owner does not emerge, the item becomes the finder's permanent property, mirroring the general rule for personal wealth. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on preserving the rights of the original owner while providing legal clarity for the finder after a reasonable period of search.
